items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Tommy Brooks started to tell me he was afraid to fly and would it be alright if he stayed in Marseille and waited for our return. I jumped sky high and told him that the Casablanca's engagement was abig affair and his name was on the contract.

ctx.x: After Paris, we did thirty three more concerts in France before flying to North Africa to do some dates. We had a concert in Marseille the 27th, and were to fly the 29th for Casablanca. There were two jazz clubs in Marseille that were enemies. So the one who was not the organiser, was trying to make scandal and keep the concert from taking place. They didn't succeed, but they cut the tyres of our bus with knives. All four of it!

The 28th, we were invited to dinner at the home of a girl that was a friend to many jazz musicians. Her name was Simone Manzi, and she had prepared a fine dinner for us, with plenty of drinks and all the works. Before the dinner, Tommy Brooks started to tell me he was afraid to fly and would it be alright if he stayed in Marseille and waited for our return. I jumped sky high and told him that the Casablanca's engagement was abig affair and his name was on the contract. He said O.K. he would come.

In the middle of the dinner, Tommy Brookins asked to be excused for a few minutes. When we finally finished the dinner and thanked Simone for a beautiful evening and left for our hotel, Tommy had not returned. At first, we thought that he has gone to the John and after we didn't see him when we left Simone, we couldn't imagine why he left the way he did.
